newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan says he does not expect Greece-Turkey war.
newsitem.headline: Annan says he does not expect Greece-Turkey war.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Thursday he did not expect a war between Greece and Turkey.

"I don't think so. I don't think there will be a war," Annan told a questioner at a news conference. "We are attempting to defuse the tensions and I think we have seen an improvement already. And I would hope none of the leaders will do anything that will escalate matters," he said.

Annan had been asked by a Greek reporter whether he agreed with a recent statement by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind about the risk of war between Greece and Turkey over Cyprus. Rifkind actually spoke of tensions over the Aegean, where the two countries almost clashed last year over an uninhabited islet.
On the Cyprus issue, Annan said there had "been a tendency to bring in armaments into the region, which does raise tensions."

He said the United Nations hoped to continue proximity talks with the leaders of the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities in the hope that "we can see enough progress and identify enough common ground for us eventually to have face-to-face talks."

"It would be preferable that the talks take place this year and ideally before September. Otherwise we are going to get into the election fever," he said, referring to elections due to be held by the Greek Cypriots early in 1998.

He urged the governments to cooperate with U.N. special representative Han Sung-joo of South Korea "and really try and bridge their differences and allow us to be able to organise face-to-face talks."
He said Britain and the United States were "working in a supportive role with us."
"The U.N. will be in the lead. The British and the American efforts will be in support," he added.

Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since Turkish troops landed in the north of the island in 1974 in response to a coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruliong Greece. The United Nations has since been trying to reunite Cyprus under a federal system.
